permissions.description: Provider operations may read/write/delete external resources, refresh OAuth tokens, send mail, access local files or mutate ONF state when deliberately executed. definitions.description: Push LogQL streams. values entries use nanosecond timestamp STRINGS plus log text; never convert timestamps to floating-point numbers.

definitions.name: Loki Query Result Decode
definitions.description: Expand Loki Query Result without losing unknown fields.
definitions.documentation:
Expand Loki Query Result without losing unknown fields.

Inputs: value (required). Outputs: resultType, result, stats, remainder.

Pure transformation; no provider requests, persistent state or credentials. Record codecs reject remainder collisions with declared fields. Missing optional fields stay absent; explicit null follows the pinned schema. List codecs select/reinsert one item at index; an empty list omits item and requires index zero. Connect only optional outputs present for your case.

Uses the exact shared Loki Query Result version. Encode output validates the complete resource schema; scalar codec ports do not weaken it.

definitions.name: Loki Get Index Statistics
definitions.description: Get Index Statistics. Query/log timestamps are strings to retain nanosecond precision. Tenant header is optional; authorization belongs to the configured proxy.
definitions.documentation:
Get Index Statistics. Query/log timestamps are strings to retain nanosecond precision. Tenant header is optional; authorization belongs to the configured proxy.

GET /loki/api/v1/index/stats. Read operation.

Inputs: query (optional), start (optional), end (optional), tenantId (optional). Missing inputs may come from the selected connection profile config or explicit node defaults. Outputs: status, request_id, operation_url, value. Optional outputs are absent when the provider omits them. HTTP202 is acceptance, not completed work; operation_url exposes a same-origin asynchronous status URL when supplied.

Setup: configure baseUrl (https://loki.example.com), bearer credentials through encrypted secret names or Connections. Default secret name: LOKI_TOKEN. Connection credentials accessToken/apiKey or username/password are resolved at execution. Never put credentials in literal inputs, baseUrl or logs. Required access: Read permission for the selected resource.

Bounds: requestTimeoutMs=15000 (100..120000), maxBytes=1048576 (1024..3000000), maxItems=1000 (1..5000), maxPages=1 (1..20). One bounded request; use the provider-specific explicit paging inputs where offered. HTTPS is required; private HTTP needs allowHttp=true. TLS validation remains enabled. Redirects, cross-origin/escaped continuation URLs and repeated continuations fail. No implicit retries. Error text contains provider/status only, never raw response bodies or credentials. Reconcile an uncertain external action before another attempt.

Synthetic example inputs:

```json
{
  "query": "{job=\"demo\"}"
}
```

This example is documentation, not a run. 

Source: https://grafana.com/docs/loki/latest/reference/loki-http-api/

definitions.name: JSON Value
definitions.description: ONF typed decoder outputs v1. Finite JSON scalar, null, typed record or typed list; arbitrary nesting is preserved.

definitions.name: JSON Record
definitions.description: ONF typed decoder outputs v1. Dynamic string-key dictionary; each value is a recursively validated JSON Value. Decode offers entries and key lookup.

definitions.name: JSON List
definitions.description: ONF typed decoder outputs v1. Ordered extensible JSON values; Decode offers typed index access.
